Marc-André Lavoie’s office at the rink (with the branch chief’s approval):

On the morning of 6 November 2030, in the compressor room of the Aréna du Parc ice rink in Mile End, the ice master Gilles Roy (61) was found dead. Heavy ammonia in the room; the relief valve open, its handle missing.

The youth team player Anika Sharma found the body at 06.10 when she saw white vapour seeping from under the compressor room door. The rink manager Marc-André Lavoie and the coach Denis Ouellet arrived at 06.20.
INCIDENT REPORT
Request the autopsy report
Request the compressor maintenance log
Request permission to search the manager’s office
Request an examination of the compressor room

· The relief valve is fully open; the handle has been removed. Without a handle the valve can’t be closed by hand.
· The door is locked from outside. The emergency mask hook is empty; the mask isn’t inside the room either.
· The plate on the compressor registered as ‘new’ has been removed and riveted back on; the year of manufacture beneath it is 1998.
COMPRESSOR ROOM EXAMINATION

The log was a decoy: the manager’s signature said he was the last person in the room, not that he was in the clear. The room examination and the coach got the search opened; the search found the handle and the mask.
He wrote ‘normal’. He forgot to erase Gilles’s line above it.
Aréna du Parc — November 2030

The manager Marc-André Lavoie made it look as though the rink’s cooling system had been ‘renewed’ and took $1.8 million; the compressor fitted was a relabelled 1998 unit. The ice master Gilles Roy saw the plate and was going to write to the city. Lavoie knocked him out in the compressor room, opened the ammonia valve and removed its handle, took the mask, locked the door and wrote ‘normal’ in the log.
Who killed Gilles Roy?
